results.fact: Shape of the lower approach (4-mile roadbed vs immediate climb)
results.correct_value: About 4 miles of old roadbed along Goodell Creek (heavy blowdown) to a cairned turnoff near 1,700 ft, then a steep climbers' path gaining roughly 4,000 ft in about 2 miles to treeline/heather benches.
results.evidence: One detailed trip report puts a stream crossing and cairned Terror Basin turnoff at about 3.5 miles and ~1,700 ft after the flat valley walk, with the steep path then climbing a spur ridge to talus near 4,000 ft and on to the 6,200 ft notch. A second climber describes four miles to the base of the hill climb, then a 4,000 ft climb in just 2 miles; a third route write-up gives ~4.5 miles of old road bed to a flat spot with cairns, then the steep climb. The approach prose (and its copy in approach_variants) started the climb at the boulder and measured the 4,000 ft from 3,200 ft; both are corrected to the roadbed-then-turnoff shape the itinerary and waypoints already use.

results.correct_value: 4th class overall: a 3rd-4th class scramble with a few 4th-class moves to an exposed summit block; no fifth-class climbing.
results.evidence: The route listing rates it 4th class, Grade II, and describes a mellow 3rd-4th class scramble up scree and talus to the exposed summit block, with no fifth-class section. Nothing found supports a 5.6 or low-fifth step, so those qualifiers are removed and the 3rd-class-only descriptions widened to 3rd-4th.
